title: Automated Lashing and Unlashing of High-Stacked Empty Containers in Seaports Using a Multi-Sensor Collaborative Robot System
content: Typhoons and severe wind events can destabilize high-stacked empty containers in container yards, creating risks to workers, handling equipment, nearby infrastructure, and the public. This study presents an automated container lashing and unlashing system intended to reduce human exposure during typhoon-preparation and recovery operations. The proposed system integrates a collaborative robot, a two-dimensional camera, a distance sensor, a gyroscope sensor, and a hook-manipulation gripper. Lashing is formulated as a vision-guided peg-in-hole insertion problem. The system detects the corner casting hole, estimates image-position error, fuses distance and angular-motion measurements, aligns the hook, inserts it, and verifies engagement. Unlashing is formulated as constrained picking and extraction. The system detects and captures the hook, manages lashing-belt tension, withdraws the hook, and verifies disengagement. The closed-loop pipeline includes target detection, relative-motion compensation, motion planning, safety monitoring, and recovery. Experiments were conducted using 50 lashing trials and 50 unlashing trials under lab test environments. The system achieved 95% of success rate for lashing and 94% of success rate for unlashing, with mean operation times of 35s and 32s, respectively. The results are intended to establish the feasibility of combining compact multi-sensor perception with collaborative-robot manipulation for container-yard safety. The principal limitations are outdoor illumination, metallic reflection, limited three-dimensional perception, indirect translational-motion estimation, and variation in hook pose and belt tension.
